newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Racist murder trial of Portuguese skinheads begins.
newsitem.headline: Racist murder trial of Portuguese skinheads begins.

text.p: The trial began on Friday of 19 skinheads accused of beating to death a young black man in a racially motivated killing which provoked outrage in Portugal.

The accused, charged with murder and grievous bodily harm, are suspected of having belonged to a group of 50 skinheads who rampaged through Lisbon in the early hours one weekend in June 1995, attacking blacks with iron rods and baseball bats.

Alcindo Monteiro, a 27-year-old Portuguese citizen of Cape Verdean origin, later died of injuries to his brain and spine and at least 12 people of African origin were injured in the attack in the Bairro Alto suburb, a popular tourist haunt.
After several delays, a Lisbon court began proceedings with a brief hearing on Friday at which 17 of the accused, aged between 17 and 38, identified themselves.
Some of them made obscene gestures at TV cameras, court sources said.

The judge accepted a request by defence lawyers to ban photographers and cameramen from broadcasting images in order to avoid sensational publicity, the sources said. Portuguese TV stations showed no pictures of the court session.
Thirteen of the 19 have been held in preventive custody since their arrest by police weeks after the killing, the sources said. Two had fled but were being tried in absentia.

The killing came during an outbreak of racial violence that shocked Portugal to the core. The country has long become accustomed to racial tolerance after the assimilation of blacks from former colonies in Africa into Portuguese society.
President Mario Soares appealed for calm among Africans in Portugal shortly after the killing.
Monteiro was a symbol of Portugal's tradition of racial integration.

Born in the Cape Verde islands off West Africa, he had spent his last 16 years in Portugal, working in an office with a record of good conduct, and carried a Portuguese national identity card, colleagues and relatives said.
Parliament held a minute's silence in his memory days after the attack which was condemned by politicians and party leaders across party lines.
Portugal, with a population of 10 million, has some 170,000 registered foreign residents.
The government has estimated there may be up to 70,000 illegal immigrants, many from former colonies, but unofficial estimates range up to 150,000 illegal immigrants.
The last major racist incident in Portugal took place in October 1989 when skinheads attacked supporters of the extreme leftwing Socialist Revolutionary Party and stabbed to death one of its leaders.
The convicted murderer, Pedro Grilo, sentenced to 12 years in jail in 1991, escaped hidden in a laundry van after serving just four months. He later surrendered himself to authorities.
The trial of the skinheads is expected to last several weeks, the court sources said.
